title: India Says Direct Taiwan Flights Will Fly Despite Pakistan Airspace Row
excerpt: Pakistan barred China Airlines and EVA Air citing the 'One China' policy, then reversed course within hours — as EVA Air prepares to launch nonstop Delhi-Taipei flights on December 1.
body:
• Pakistan barred Taiwan's China Airlines and EVA Air from its airspace citing Beijing's 'One China' policy, then reversed course within hours, granting both carriers overflight permission from October 28, 2026 to March 27, 2027.
  • India's foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said direct India-Taiwan flights would not be derailed: "My sense is, if there are direct flights, they will fly."
  • For travellers: EVA Air starts nonstop Taipei-Delhi flights on December 1, 2026 — five times a week on Airbus A330-300s, bookings already open — restoring a direct link last served in early 2020.
  • Indian passport holders with a valid or recently expired US, UK, Schengen, Japanese, Korean, Australian, New Zealand or Canadian visa can apply online, free, for a Taiwan Travel Authorization Certificate (90-day validity, 14-day stay per entry).

India's Ministry of External Affairs said on Wednesday that planned direct flights between India and Taiwan would go ahead, hours after Pakistan first barred Taiwanese airlines from its airspace in the name of Beijing's 'One China' policy and then reversed the decision. Asked whether the Pakistan move would affect the planned services, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told a press briefing: "My sense is, if there are direct flights, they will fly," according to reports of the briefing carried by The Times of India and Hindustan Times.

"The aviation division follows the One China policy — only mainland China is allowed. We have permitted only Chinese airlines to fly over Pakistan."

— Khawaja Asif, Pakistan Defence Minister, to Bloomberg News

A ban, then a same-day reversal

Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif told Bloomberg News that the country's aviation division followed the 'One China' policy and had permitted only mainland Chinese airlines to overfly Pakistan. Bloomberg reported Pakistan was the first country to take such a step explicitly in support of Beijing's position that Taiwan is part of China. Flight-tracking data cited by Bloomberg and Pakistani media showed the effect was already visible before the announcement: neither China Airlines nor EVA Air had crossed Pakistan since the morning of October 25, and at least a dozen of their Asia-Europe services had rerouted over Russia. On October 24 alone, the two carriers had operated 14 flights through Pakistani airspace.

Within hours, the position changed. Documents reviewed by Dawn and reported by Bloomberg showed Pakistan's Civil Aviation Authority had authorised both carriers to use its airspace from October 28, 2026 through March 27, 2027. No official explanation for the reversal was given. The detour had not been cost-free: routings over Russia and alternative paths through South Asia and the Middle East added hours to some journeys and raised fuel burn, and Taiwanese carriers had generally avoided Russian airspace since February 2022. Reports also noted the original restriction went further than Beijing itself — China allows Taiwanese airlines to use its airspace.

Why the Delhi-Taipei route matters

The flight at the centre of the exchange is EVA Air's new nonstop Taipei-Delhi service, which begins December 1, 2026. EVA will operate five flights a week with Airbus A330-300 aircraft — flight BR367 departs Taipei at 11:00 and arrives in Delhi at 15:35, while BR368 leaves Delhi at 19:55 and lands in Taipei at 04:20 the next day — making it the only Taiwan-based airline offering nonstop passenger flights to India. China Airlines last served the market nonstop until early 2020, at two flights a week, so the new schedule more than doubles the previous frequency.

Demand has grown in the gap. About 158,500 passengers travelled between Taiwan and India in 2025, up 25.8% from roughly 126,000 in 2024 and 20.4% above 2019, according to Sabre data reported by Aviation Week. With no nonstop option, more than 98% of those passengers connected en route, mainly through Bangkok, Hong Kong and Singapore. EVA Air President Clay Sun said growing manufacturing, semiconductor, AI and technology ties are driving the route, and the airline's partnership with Air India offers onward connections beyond Delhi, while Taipei connects Indian travellers to EVA's North American network.

What travellers should do

Bookings for the December 1 launch are open on EVA Air's website and through travel agencies. For entry, Indian nationals who hold a valid visa or residence card — or one expired within the last 10 years — from the United States, United Kingdom, Schengen area, Japan, Korea, Australia, New Zealand or Canada can apply online for a free ROC Travel Authorization Certificate instead of a regular visa; the certificate is valid for 90 days, allows multiple entries and permits a stay of 14 days per entry, and the passport must be valid for at least six months from arrival. Travellers booked on Taiwanese carriers' Europe services should also check their routings: the overflight permission runs only to March 27, 2027, and a lapse would mean longer routings again.

What happens after March 2027 is the open question. Pakistan has not explained either the ban or its reversal, and the five-month permission leaves the longer-term status of Taiwanese overflights unresolved. For now, India's position is the simpler one: the direct flights are a commercial service, and they will fly.
